cancer patients with shorter telomeres exhibit higher sensitivity to mutagens in PBL and that this association is particularly strong in CRC patients.
CRC patients exhibit increased mutagen sensitivity and shorter RTL compared with controls, whereas no differences were observed in BC patients.
CRC patients are more sensitive to DNA damage induced by bleomycine than controls, and that telomere shorting is associated with higher bleomycine‐induced chromosmal aberrations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possible role of telomeres and DNA repair capacity in the etiology of CRC and BC.
a possible role of telomere length in the etiopathogenesis of cancers.
the role of telomere shortness and DSB repair deficiency in cancer initiation.

the increased mutagen sensitivity of CRC patients is associated with the shortening of telomeress.
telomere shortness may be a risk factor for CRC and BC, but not for other cancer types.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the observed increased mutagen sensitivity and shortened telomeres in cancer patients may be a result of the altered DNA repair capacity in cancer cells.

The main takeaway from our work is that
cancer patients with shortened telomeres and deficient DNA repair capacity are at higher risk for developing secondary cancers.
the measurement of bleomycin‐inducted chromosomal damage in PBL may be used as a biomarker of cancer risk.
